name: four-tile-wide stone-edged canal, 3/4 top-down: on each bank a flight of stone quay steps descending south into the water (landing at bank level, treads and risers, last step submerged), and a canal lock across the canal (plank walkway with iron railing on top of two iron-banded wooden lock gates, water spilling from sluices, a wooden capstan on each bank)
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_canal

surfaces.part: canal water, full-height channel
stone quay steps on both banks (pale blocks with tread and riser bands, landing, submerged last step)
lock plank walkway with iron railing posts
iron-banded wooden lock gates with sluice spill
wooden capstans on the banks
grass and cobblestone bank strips

answer.evidence: The main body is a canal drawn as a flat plan view: water, grass and cobble strips run the full 176 rows with no south face. The only vertical faces are small details. The lock gates have a front of about 6 rows (64-69) under the walkway top at rows 58-63. The quay steps are pale blocks seen mostly from above, with small tread and riser bands. The canal is a terrain surface with no standing volume, so I measured it as top-down.

styleAnswer.evidence: Candidate has 4 visible tones per tile against 7 for the paving reference (the grass reference shows 3, but with real tuft clustering). The grass is a flat mid-green with sparse tuft marks repeated in an obvious pattern. The paving band is uniform dark grey cobble with little per-stone shading, unlike the reference's lit stone joints. The water is a flat teal with a few rain streaks. The quay steps are small pale blocks with only 2-3 steps of shading, and the lock walkway is a simple plank strip. Thin grey edge lines run down both banks. 53% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is near-black or grey in places. Near-flat coverage is 18% against 0% for both references, so large areas are flat fills. The piece is readable but shallower and flatter than the Beodeul ground standard.

answer.evidence: This is a terrain block. Most of it (water, grass, cobble) is flat ground seen from above. The one built volume is the lock. Its plank walkway (rows 116-126, with railing posts) ends in a dark front-edge line at row 126. Below that are the iron-banded wooden gate faces (rows 127-138) with sluice spill and foam (rows 138-144). The quay steps show treads and risers, but they are only loosely 3/4. The lock is the only volume with a top surface and a front face of 3+ rows, so I read it as three_quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has about 4 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Its grass is a flat mid green with sparse tuft marks, and 18% of it is near-flat where the references have 0%. The stone steps are pale blocks with only 2-3 steps of shading, no per-stone detail and little texture. The canal water is a mostly flat teal with a few streaks. The cobble bank is a uniform dark grey speckle, much less varied than the reference paving, which has cut slabs and mortar lines. The lock is a brown plank strip with minimal grain, and the capstans are tiny blobs. Dark edge pixels are 53% neutral, so the outline is mixed: the grey/black bank lines look sticker-like, while the stone pieces use some tinted edges. Overall it reads shallower and flatter than the Beodeul references.

answer.evidence: The main body is a flat top-down map. Water, grass and cobble fill rows 0-175 and show no vertical south face; the column scan at x=80 shows only water-colour stripes with no edge line or front face. The quay steps are drawn as flat stone blocks with thin horizontal bands, and the last step fades into the water. Only the lock has a short vertical face, the gate planks and sluices at about rows 127-137, but that is a small detail on a flat canal. This is the normal look of terrain tiles.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a canal with quay steps and a lock, and the references are grass and paving, so the kind matches. Grass is a flat mid-green with sparse tuft marks, about 3 steps against the reference's tufts and dark patch. 18% near-flat coverage against 0% in both references shows real flat fills in the grass and in the water. Its 4 visible tones per tile beat the grass reference's 3 but fall well short of the paving's 7. The cobble bank is only 2-3 greys with a grey-black lean. The stone steps are pale and nearly white, with a few lines and little per-stone shading. The wooden lock deck has some plank detail, but the gates, sluices and capstans are small and simple. Edge pixels are 53% neutral, which is between the references, so the outline looks like a mix of near-black grey and tinted lines. The water has streak texture but only 2-3 teal tones, so it looks shallower than Beodeul's ramps. Overall it is clean but thinner and flatter than the references.
